title: One char, two conversions
request: Teach me what printf("%f", (double)a) does to a char.

claims.text: The program stores 'B' in the char a, then prints a with %d and (double)a with %f.
claims.justification: Lines 4 to 6 of fcast.c do exactly this, in this order.

claims.text: On this platform the character constant 'B' has the value 66, its code in ASCII and in UTF-8.
claims.justification: C17 leaves the values of execution characters to the implementation. Apple clang encodes 'B' as the single byte 66, which is its code in ASCII and in UTF-8, and the captured %d line shows 66.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: The values of the members of the execution character set are implementation-defined.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: The value of an integer character constant containing a single character that maps to a single-byte execution character is the numerical value of the representation of the mapped character interpreted as an integer.

claims.text: In printf("%d\n", a), the char a is promoted to int before the call, so %d receives the int 66 and prints 66.
claims.justification: a is a trailing argument of a variadic call, so the default argument promotions apply and char becomes int; %d then prints that int in decimal.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: The ellipsis notation in a function prototype declarator causes argument type conversion to stop after the last declared parameter. The default argument promotions are performed on trailing arguments.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: the integer promotions are performed on each argument, and arguments that have type float are promoted to double. These are called the default argument promotions.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: d,i The int argument is converted to signed decimal in the style [−]dddd.

claims.text: The cast (double)a converts the value 66 to the double 66.0 before printf is called, so %f receives a double and prints 66.000000.
claims.justification: A cast converts the value of its operand to the named type. 66 is exactly representable as a double, so the result is 66.0, and %f prints a double with six digits after the point by default.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: Preceding an expression by a parenthesized type name converts the value of the expression to the named type.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: When a value of integer type is converted to a real floating type, if the value being converted can be represented exactly in the new type, it is unchanged.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: f,F A double argument representing a floating-point number is converted to decimal notation in the style [−]ddd.ddd, where the number of digits after the decimal-point character is equal to the precision specification. If the precision is missing, it is taken as 6

claims.text: Without the cast, printf("%f\n", a) would pass an int where %f expects a double, which is undefined behaviour.
claims.justification: The default argument promotions turn the char into an int, and %f needs a double argument; a wrong argument type for a conversion specification is undefined behaviour.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: If any argument is not the correct type for the corresponding conversion specification, the behavior is undefined.

claims.text: Pause here and predict what %f prints before you go on.
claims.justification: A prompt for the learner; it makes no technical statement.

misconceptions.statement: %d prints the letter B because a is a char.
